[[File:CadBaneGauntlets-FFp5.png|thumb|left|200px|Cad Bane's gauntlets were a deadly part of Bane's arsenal.]] The bulk of Bane's miniaturized equipment, which allowed him to hide his weapons in plain sight, was inspired by that of a Hutt enforcer who used it to imitate a Jedi. His durasteel magno-grip boots were equipped with customized [[Mitrinomon jetpack thruster]]s, which granted him flight over long periods in low-gravity environments and also gave him an aerial advantage in situations like the zero-gravity battle aboard his frigate. One rocket thruster was strong enough to propel him through the air, as was the case during his confrontation with Anakin Skywalker on Orondia. Although his custom-made multipurpose wrist gauntlets were the most bulky and noticeable items that he wore, they hid a variety of control devices, built-in tools, and weapons, including a [[cable launcher]], [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]], [[data uplink]], lanyard, and non-lethal contact [[Stunner/Legends|stunners]] that could subdue targets even as large as [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]]. His gauntlets were also capable of remote control and could operate starship functions, from controls aboard his ''Munificent''-class star frigate and a [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]] to those aboard his personal Telgorn dropship, the ''Sleight of Hand'', or his starfighter, the ''Xanadu Blood''. To top it off, each of his gauntlets was equipped with a projectile launcher and a flamethrower, which he sometimes used in place of his blasters. Bane's gear in general was designed to counteract the abilities of Force-users: his external breathing tubes prevented him from being Force-choked; his rocket boots rivaled a Jedi's [[Force speed/Legends|Force speed]] and Force leaps, allowing him to outpace and outjump Force-users; and his contact stunners were meant to electrocute foes in an imitation of [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]]. His usual choice of clothing included a wide-brimmed hat and a [[nashtah]]-hide tunic with a heavy cloak, an outfit that became his trademark appearance.{{TCWA|set=Cad Bane}} For head gear, he preferred a hat to a helmet, the latter of which he refused to hide under in spite of its extra protection. His penchant for hats tended to stand out, leading those who were familiar with him, such as Skywalker and Ahsoka Tano, to recognize him even when he was not sporting his trademark equipment. While on the run from Republic authorities with Moralo Eval, Bane was forced to select new gear from Pablo's Pawnshop. He chose a light vest while making sure to acquire rocket boots and a new hat, which he later exchanged for his prized wide-brimmed hat from Bulduga, who had come into possession of it. In addition, he obtained gauntlets that retained some of the functions of his usual ones, such as a cable launcher, while also incorporating a knockout gas dispenser. For weaponry, he secured a GALAAR-15 blaster carbine in addition to a familiar LL-30 blaster pistol, along with holsters to carry both. As far as droid assistance went, Bane used Todo 360, an incredibly useful techno-service droid who was equipped with a number of built-in gadgets,{{SWArchive|url=clonewars/tradingcards/cards/lg_todo360.jpg|text=Clone Card: Todo 360}} for various missions and jobs. Bane viewed him as a "butler droid," despite the droid's resentment of being classified as such. At one point, Bane sacrificed Todo as a distraction to escape from the Jedi Temple, but the droid was later reconstructed and returned to serve him. Bane additionally used several deadly IG-86 sentinel droids in his operations because of the line's agility and intelligence,{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Clone Wars (toy line)|pack=(Target Exclusive) Cad Bane & IG-86|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TCWEXCadBane-IG86.asp}} often relying on them for muscle to supplement the skills of other mercenaries in his work. Among their number were HELIOS-3D and HELIOS-3E,{{SWArchive|url=clonewars/tradingcards/cards/lg_helios3e.jpg|text=Clone Card: HELIOS-3E}} who were both originally owned by Ziro the Hutt. [[File:XanaduBlood-NabooCOTF.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The heavily modified ''Xanadu Blood'' served as Bane's starfighter on a number of operations.]] For transportation, Bane piloted a number of modified starships for his operations. He utilized the ''Sleight of Hand'', a Telgorn dropship with formidable weapons and defensive systems that he personally outfitted with military-grade gear and an advanced hyperdrive to suit his needs as a transport vessel. The dropship was equipped with a tractor beam as well as deflector shields, the latter of which were powerful enough to minimize damage and even prevent the pilot from being aware of collisions with other starships. A sophisticated [[Sensor jammer/Legends|sensor jammer]] even rendered the dropship invisible to most [[scanner]]s. Bane also flew the ''Xanadu Blood'', a heavily modified ''Rogue''-class starfighter that he acquired from Darth Sidious. Although its layers of paint were chipped, the fighter served Bane's purposes in his hunt for Force-sensitive infants. Despite the fact that he lost possession of both of his starships on various occasions, he eventually retrieved both of them. ==Behind the scenes== ===Portrayal=== {{Quote|The crew loves Cad Bane, and I really think the fans will, too. He brings a serious bad-ass sensibility to ''Star Wars''. He's a lethal and ruthless bounty hunter, and you see that right away in the episode. Unlike Boba Fett, Cad doesn't take prisoners.|[[Giancarlo Volpe]], director of Bane's debut episode, "Hostage Crisis"|}} [[File:Wide-brimmed_hat_bounty_hunter.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The bounty hunter concept art upon which Bane's model was based]] The character of Cad Bane was created for the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series. He was first featured in [[March]] [[2009]] in the series' [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]] finale, "[[Hostage Crisis]]," as well as in its accompanying [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (webcomics)|webcomic]], [[The Clone Wars: Invitation Only|''Invitation Only'']]. Because the episode introduced the role of bounty hunters into the series, Bane was one of the first such individuals to appear in the show. He also appeared in [[The Clone Wars: Hunting the Hunters (Part I)|''Hunting the Hunters, Part I'']], the first in a sub-series of ''The Clone Wars'' [[Star Wars comic books|webcomics]] that transitioned between the television series' first and [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second]] seasons, and became a prominent character in [[Ryder Windham]]'s [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Secret Missions|''Secret Missions'']] novel series, which was released from 2009 to [[2012]]. As of [[August]] [[2010]], he was voted the thirty-first most popular character in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] on [http://www.ign.com/star-wars-characters/index.html IGN.com].{{WebCite|url=http://www.ign.com/star-wars-characters/31.html|text=Cad Bane - #31 Star Wars Character - IGN|format=Online article|work=[http://www.ign.com/star-wars-characters/index.html Top 100 Star Wars Characters]|archivedate=20130615104946}} Thanks to his instant popularity with the [[Lucasfilm Animation]] crew, Bane was featured in the three-part story arc—comprised of the episodes "[[Holocron Heist]]," "[[Cargo of Doom]]," and "[[Children of the Force]]"—that began the series' Season Two in [[October]] 2009. In addition to appearing in [[The Clone Wars: Act on Instinct|''Act on Instinct'']], the season's accompanying webcomic, he was given roles in the multi-platform [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Republic Heroes]]'' and in [[Cartoon Network]]'s [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Game Creator|''The Clone Wars Game Creator'']].{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news20091012/index.html|text=Cartoon Network Launches ''Star Wars'' Game Creator Online}} In 2010, Bane was [[Galaxy at War (Star Wars Miniatures)|collected]] in the ''[[Star Wars Miniatures]]'' line{{SWArchive|url=games/othergames/news20091009/index.html|text=Enemy Forces in Galaxy at War}} and in several of [[Hasbro]]'s [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (toy line)|toy lines]].{{SWArchive|url=vault/collecting/news20100223.html|text=Hasbro Toy Fair Round Up!}} He returned to the television series in the [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|third season]] episodes "[[Evil Plans]]" and "[[Hunt for Ziro]]," which aired in [[November]] 2010 as prequels and sequels, respectively, to "Hostage Crisis." In [[December]] 2010, Bane was featured in his very own [[StarWars.com]] game, entitled ''[[Cad Bane: Jedi Hunter]]''. He began to be featured in [[Spices & Spies|several]] [[Outgunned|comics]] released as part of the [[Star Wars Comic|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic UK'']] publication, and in [[2011]], he received a role in the non-canonical video game ''[[LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars]]''.''[[LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars]]'' Throughout ''The Clone Wars'' television series and in ''Republic Heroes'', Bane was portrayed by voice actor [[Corey Burton]], who also provided the voices for Shahan Alama, Ziro Desilijic Tiure, and Count Dooku in the series. At the suggestion of Series Producer and ''Star Wars'' creator [[George Lucas]], Burton took inspiration from film actor [[Wikipedia:Peter Lorre|Peter Lorre]] in voicing Bane and used the character's pre-established [[Wikipedia:American Old West|Western American]] influences to bring the bounty hunter to life with his own original characterization.{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news20090320.html|text=Corey Burton: Voicing Villains}} Portraying Bane as a "transplanted [[Wikipedia:European American|European immigrant]] in the Old West" who had adjusted to the local dialect, Burton was also influenced by a few contemporary actors who had played soft-spoken cinematic heavies, including [[Wikipedia:Humphrey Bogart|Humphrey Bogart]] and [[Wikipedia:Robert Mitchum|Robert Mitchum]]. Burton's voice was additionally modified on the computer by the series' sound production team before being set in the final version of each television episode.''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Official Episode Guide: Season 1]]'' ===Development=== Initially, bounty hunters were not to be a part of the television series, but as the first season's storylines developed, a character was required to fill the role of a hunter. Supervising Director [[Dave Filoni]] and writer [[Henry Gilroy]] explored the possibility of bringing the [[Gen'Dai/Legends|Gen'Dai]] mercenary [[Durge/Legends|Durge]] into the series, and the character was re-imagined as a [[Human/Legends|Human]]. The individual evolved into one named "Nom Kahbah" before Lucas became personally involved with the development, suggesting that a Western American influence be used. At Lucas's request, inspiration for the character was taken from actor [[Wikipedia:Lee Van Cleef|Lee Van Cleef's]] performances in the films [[Wikipedia:The Good, the Bad and the Ugly|''The Good, the Bad and the Ugly'']] and [[Wikipedia:For a Few Dollars More|''For a Few Dollars More'']]. Filoni found an unlabeled sketch of a bounty hunter from the [[Original trilogy|original ''Star Wars'' trilogy]], and the resultant creation was Bane, whose model drew from the concept art with additional expansion by Lead Designer [[Kilian Plunkett]] to incorporate the Duros [[Species/Legends|species]]' features. Lucas eventually changed the character's name to "Cad Bane," paving the way for Bane's place in ''Star Wars'' canon. According to some early layout animation scenes released in [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|The Complete Season Two's]] Blu-ray "Jedi Temple Archives" feature, Bane originally escaped from the ''Resolute'' at the end of the episode "Cargo of Doom." An alternate ending to the episode also showed him contacting Viceroy Nute Gunray and opening the activated Jedi holocron, accessing the list of Force-sensitive infants stored within the Kyber memory crystal.[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Two]], "Jedi Temple Archives" Blu-ray feature for "[[Cargo of Doom]]" That ending was removed from the final version of the episode, as Bane instead escaped from the ''Resolute'' at the beginning of the following episode, "Children of the Force." In November [[2013]], following the end of the television series earlier that year, Series Writer [[Brent Friedman]]—who scripted the Season Four arc that featured Bane—indicated in an [http://rebelsreport.com/2013/11/22/rebels-report-2-behind-the-scenes-with-brent-friedman interview] that more episodes featuring the character had been written and would have been released in future seasons.{{WebCite|url=http://rebelsreport.com/2013/11/22/rebels-report-2-behind-the-scenes-with-brent-friedman|text=Rebels Report #2: Behind the Scenes with Brent Friedman|date=2013-11-22|quote=[starting around 54:27] I know [Cad Bane]'s a beloved character, and certainly as Season Five ended, his fate was not determined. But I also know that there were episodes that were written in what would have been Season Six, Seven, and Eight where we had some really interesting plans for him—fairly surprising plans.|archivedate=20131128121240}} One such story was a four-episode arc written by Series Head Writer [[Matt Michnovetz]] that brought Bane into contact with a young Boba Fett.{{SW|url=news/swca-the-untold-clone-wars-panel-liveblog|text=SWCA: The Untold ''Clone Wars'' Panel Liveblog}}{{Twitter|MattMichnovetz|status/341245477838266368|[[Matt Michnovetz]]|archivefile=File:Michnovetz-YouBet.png}} The arc would have consisted of a team-up for a "rescue mission" on Tatooine where [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] had kidnapped a child. It would have emphasized Fett's and Bane's relation to one another, as Bane had known Fett's father. Bane would also get new [[Clothing/Legends|clothes]] and a new ship called the ''[[Justifier]]''.{{SWYouTube|7yKM6RExLlI|The Untold Clone Wars Panel | Star Wars Celebration Anaheim}} In a clip revealed during the Animated Origins and Unexpected Fates panel at [[Celebration Orlando]] in [[2017]], Bane and other bounty hunters had ended an insurrection by Fett. To finish it, they would have engaged in a stand-off duel.{{SWYouTube|85Jw-63YNYI|Star Wars Celebration Orlando 2017: Animated Origins and Unexpected Fates}} ===Inconsistencies=== {{Quote|However, it seems that not everyone was pleased to see Ziro locked away. While it's not clear from this episode who was responsible, someone of considerable means must have hired bounty hunter Cad Bane and his team to rescue the Hutt. And from Chancellor Palpatine's exchange with Bane (where he warns the bounty hunter, 'You will end up paying for this outrage'), it seems doubtful that the Separatists are behind this rescue, either. But then again, Darth Sidious's mysterious plans have never been easy to unravel.|The open-ended excerpt from ''The Official Episode Guide: Season 1''|}} [[File:Bane_and_Ziro.png|thumb|left|250px|The party who hired Bane to free Ziro was left unidentified for over a year.]] The party—left unnamed in 2009's "Hostage Crisis"—who had hired Bane to free Ziro the Hutt from prison was not clarified for quite some time. According to Bane's StarWars.com [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry, some first season publicity materials mistakenly implied that Darth Sidious and the Separatists had hired Bane to free Ziro.{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news20090317.html|text=The Chilling Season Finale Introduces a Deadly New Enemy}} Although the Databank entry went on to state that Bane was working for the Hutts when he liberated Ziro, the 2009 ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Official Episode Guide: Season 1]]'' publication further complicated the matter by claiming that Bane's employer had yet to be identified in Season Two, though none of the episodes featuring Bane even alluded to the Senate hostage crisis. The issue was finally resolved in the 2010 third season episode "Evil Plans," which solidified the Databank's claim that the Hutts had hired Bane, despite Jabba the Hutt's grudge against Ziro. Furthermore, an [[in-universe]] explanation for the mistaken involvement of the Separatists was provided in the 2012 ''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Updated and Expanded]]'', which stated that the Hutts had framed the Confederacy for Bane's actions. The storyline of the [[Wikipedia:Nintendo DS|Nintendo DS]] edition of ''Republic Heroes''''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Republic Heroes]]'' [[Wikipedia:Nintendo DS|Nintendo DS]] edition greatly contradicts the plot of episodes within the television series' first season,{{TCW|Lair of Grievous}} as well as the other editions of ''Republic Heroes''. In the DS edition, Bane contacts the Republic from a Separatist prison on Ryloth, where he is being held, and offers to sell information about a secret Confederate facility, but insists on only dealing with Senator Padmé Amidala. The Jedi believe the bounty hunter's information to be critical in uncovering a large Separatist plot and decide to rescue Bane, sending Jedi Master [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]] as Amidala's escort. The two infiltrate the prison and rescue Bane, but Fisto gets separated from the senator in the process. Bane promises to reveal the information if Amidala takes him to his ship, the ''Xanadu Blood'', and they fight through battle droids before eventually reaching the craft. Sticking to his word, Bane tells the senator of [[Juma 9]]—which, in this case, is a strategic Confederate outpost, while in the other editions of the game it is an active Republic [[Mining/Legends|mining]] facility. It is protected by a defense perimeter, which can only be bypassed with recent Separatist clearance codes. This leads into a storyline involving the Confederate General Grievous's castle on the third moon of Vassek that ignores the plot and aims of the [[Mission to Grievous's castle/Legends|Jedi raid]] on the lair already portrayed in the television series' first season. Because of this story's extremely conflicting plot that would otherwise require too much [[Fanon|fan-based speculation]] to integrate into the canonical biography, this article assumes that the Nintendo DS edition of ''Republic Heroes'' is non-canonical. ===Non-canon history=== {{Quote|Robot, I can't hunt down prey if my sandwich order is wrong.''"
[Bane throws a sandwich tray]
"''I distinctly ordered light mayo.''"
"''Got it.''"
[C-3PO dislodges one of Bane's breathing tubes]

"''I'll stick them back in.''"
[C-3PO places one of Bane's breathing tubes on his face]
"''I'll get you.|Cad Bane and C-3PO|{{YodaChronicles|Menace of the Sith}}}} The publication ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.15|Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic UK 6.15]]'' introduced an [[Infinities]]—non-canonical—version of the episode "Hostage Crisis." While Bane and the others are put behind bars, Amidala goes on to train to become a Jedi.[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.15|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Comic 6.15]] In the [[LEGO]] online comic ''[[Jedi Journal Entry #968]]'', Bane is in a cantina on a remote outlaw world, counting his credits from his last bounty, when General Grievous arrives. Grievous hires him to track down Jedi Master [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]], who is after the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] general, but Bane fulfills the job by simply pointing out Koon and Jedi Knight [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]] when they enter the cantina, searching for Grievous. While Grievous and IG-86 [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droids]] battle the Jedi in a firefight, Bane simply sits back and watches the show. After Grievous flees from the cantina, Bane is hired by several battle droids to hunt down R2-D2, and he calls in several of his mercenary accomplices to assist him in the gambit.''[[Jedi Journal Entry #968]]'' In addition to presenting more humorous and comical depictions of Bane in "Hostage Crisis," the ''LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars'' video game also modified the episode's storyline. In the game, Ziro the Hutt directly hires Bane to free him from prison, without the involvement of the Hutt Council. The level featuring the Senate hostage crisis ends after the Republic Executive Building's power generator is shut down. Besides being a playable character in that level, Bane can be bought as an in-game character following the "[[Petranaki arena|Geonosian Arena]]" level, for use in the game's "Free Play" mode. In the Nintendo DS edition, he is available for play after the game's "[[Blue Shadow Virus (episode)|Blue Shadow Virus]]" level.''[[LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars]]'' [[Wikipedia:Nintendo DS|Nintendo DS]] As part of the non-canonical character matchups presented in ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Head-to-Head]]'', Bane is assigned to capture [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], the leader of the Mandalorian [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]]. After tracking down Vizsla, Bane releases explosive charges to rattle his enemy, who draws the ancient weapon known as the [[Darksaber/Legends|Darksaber]]. Bane ultimately emerges victorious in the grueling confrontation that ensues, though only barely. In the 2013 video game [[LEGO Star Wars: The Yoda Chronicles (video game)|''LEGO Star Wars: The Yoda Chronicles'']], Bane is one of the selectable characters during the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|Dark Side]] campaign in the [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] missions, along with Jango Fett and the Sith clone [[Jek-14/Legends|Jek-14]]. He also appears in one of the Dark Side bonus missions, leading three B2 super battle droids against the Republic forces in never-ending waves. In the Light Side campaign's third Geonosis mission, Bane is one of the participants in the final duel in the Petranaki arena.[[LEGO Star Wars: The Yoda Chronicles (video game)|''LEGO Star Wars: The
